Module alias conventions: say which name each module is bound under, get `CP006`
when it is not, and let `--fix` write and rename bindings to match.

### Breaking (on 0.x, a minor bump is the breaking-change signal)

- `CP006` is a new finding that makes the run exit `1`, and ruff's
  `flake8-import-conventions` aliases are read by default: a project already carrying
  that ruff table can start exiting `1` with no other change (`ruff_aliases = false`
  restores the old behaviour).

### Highlights

- `[[tool.cleanporter.alias]]` rules (exact names, `*`/`**` patterns, `{leaf}` templates,
  `importer`/`file` scoping) and the `CP006` finding, in every output format.
- `--fix` names the bindings it writes by the conventions (`import numpy as np`) and
  renames a `CP006` binding at every reference, declining the file when it cannot prove it safe.
- Ruff's `flake8-import-conventions` `aliases`/`extend-aliases` act as default rules.
- `--fix` safety: no binding under a builtin's name, no read of a rewritten name left unqualified,
  no reuse of a binding that may not have run, and none a wildcard import can rebind.
- PEP 695 type aliases (`type Kind = int`) resolve: importing one is the `CP001` object
  import it always was, not a `CP002`.

Full details: [CHANGELOG.md, 0.6.0](https://github.com/grAItools/cleanporter/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#060---2026-10-07)
